comment: The CLI the copilot is, and what it offers before it is asked. Shared because both processes need it: electron/ai.js decides what it will spawn, src/models.js decides what the dropdown shows, and two copies of that is how the two disagree. Same arrangement as vault-contract.json and zoom-steps.json. `command` is the binary spawned — one process per turn, with the vault as its working directory. There is no HTTP client here and no key of ours to keep: every model, and every gateway (OpenRouter, z.ai), is reached by configuring it inside opencode, where its key already lives. `fallbacks` is what the dropdown shows before the CLI has been asked — a seed, not a limit, because the catalogue is an account property this file cannot check a name against, so what the panel offers is what gets spawned. `offerByDefault` is false because opencode's four hundred-odd entries are what the Models-offered setting exists to keep out of the dropdown. `auth` is the argument list that answers whether the CLI is signed in. `grants` is what it can actually do in the read-only or write-capable provider mode, in the user's words: it takes no per-tool allowlist, so it is fenced only by that mode — the UI's Ask and Auto choices decide whether write access is confirmed first.

grants.read: read and search your notes, and fetch web pages
grants.ask: read, edit and create notes, run shell commands inside the vault, and fetch web pages
grants.auto: read, edit and create notes, run shell commands anywhere on this Mac, and fetch web pages
